clue.text: Deal with question raised on the field of play

parts.note: to deal with a topic is to cover it
a question raised in debate is a point

explanation.surface: Someone handles an objection raised during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: COVER POINT is a fielding position in cricket, off-side of the batsman, so it is a place on the field of play.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this is a named fielding position, a spot occupied by a player during the game.

clue.text: Firm kiss above a bone

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting above another comes before it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
X is the cross used for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A firm kiss planted above a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the anatomical name for the hip, or the first segment of an insect's leg.

clue.text: Lady Virginia left lake

parts.note: VA is the US state abbreviation for Virginia
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia abandoned a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so the name of a lady.

clue.text: Get out of top gear

parts.note: reads like shifting down from the fastest gear in a car, but top gear is headwear and getting out of it means taking it off

explanation.definitionFit: Top gear is cheekily read as headgear, and getting out of it is baring the head.

clue.text: Antiquated boots Lee redesigned

indicators.note: something redesigned is put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned boots that a man called Lee has given a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges the letters of BOOTS and LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something out of date and no longer in use.

clue.text: There isn't a safety device for this group of performers

parts.note: no means there is none
a net catches acrobats who fall

explanation.surface: Performers who work without a safety net beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine musicians, like a trio or quartet but larger.

clue.text: Not all of the gin has been returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for gin is read backwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for catching game

explanation.surface: Some of the gin has been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been returned' turns TRAP round. 'gin' looks like the drink but is a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion of something is a fraction, not the whole of it.

clue.text: Eggs brought up to rotter who had nothing more than a pear

indicators.note: in a down clue bringing a word up means reading it from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: ova are eggs, the Latin plural of ovum
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who only had a pear is sick with eggs coming back up.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit is often called an alligator pear or by its own name followed by pear, so it is something beyond a plain pear.

clue.text: Edward produces toys

parts.note: Teddy is a pet form of the name Edward
to bear is to produce, as a tree bears fruit

explanation.surface: A man called Edward makes playthings.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stuffed cuddly playthings named after Theodore Roosevelt.

clue.text: Some waxy lemon tree's woody tissue

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lemon with a waxy skin and the woody part of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the botanical term for the plant tissue that carries water up a stem, forming wood.

clue.text: Composure if dragon's in a whirl

indicators.note: something in a whirl is spun about, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of dragon's, keeping the S

explanation.surface: Keeping calm if a dragon is spinning round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a whirl' rearranges IF DRAGONS; here the 'S is a letter of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for coolness under pressure, literally cold blood.

clue.text: When racers start at the beginning

definitions.meaning: a race begins when the starter calls the signal word
an idiom for right from the start

explanation.surface: Runners begin their race at the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the moment the starter's call is given, and idiomatically from the very outset.

clue.text: Rebel going round in circles

definitions.meaning: an insurgent who wants to overthrow a government

explanation.surface: An insurgent who keeps going round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent overturning the state, and something rotating like a wheel.

clue.text: Chief officer in the main

parts.note: 'in the main' seems to mean mostly, but the main is the open ocean, and the chief officer there commands a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the ocean, and the commander of a ship is its chief officer.

clue.text: Visionary by gum!

parts.note: 'by gum' looks like an exclamation, but read literally it is something set in the gums with a link to sight

explanation.definitionFit: The canine tooth sits in the gum and is named for lying beneath the organ of sight.

clue.text: Goes to remake butt

indicators.note: to remake is to build again differently, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to reshoot a film about a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remake' rearranges GOES TO. 'butt' is the butt of a joke, not a bottom or a cigarette end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is the target of jokes or who is used by others is a dupe.

clue.text: Not worth considering wasting time

definitions.meaning: fooling about idly, frittering away hours

explanation.surface: Idling away hours is hardly worth thinking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb trifle: to dally idly, and the adjective meaning trivial or paltry.

clue.text: Are horse-flies caught in it?

parts.note: horse-flies seem to be the biting insects, but split up the clue suggests a horse joined to something that traps flies

explanation.definitionFit: A spider's snare catches flies, and its name begins with a sturdy short-legged horse.

clue.text: Flat? One won't be after such a big meal

definitions.meaning: a flat tyre, one that has burst

definitions.text: One won't be after such a big meal
definitions.meaning: one's stomach will not be flat after a huge feast

explanation.surface: Feeling flat after eating far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst tyre leaves a car with a flat, and a slap-up feast leaves no one with a flat stomach.

clue.text: Stopper used to protect electrical apparatus

definitions.meaning: something that halts or checks motion
a lightning device diverts surges away from equipment

explanation.surface: A plug fitted to guard electrical gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one that stops or halts something, and a lightning device that diverts dangerous surges to earth.

clue.text: Storm on stage

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's last play, about Prospero's island

explanation.surface: A gale blowing during a theatre show.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent gale, and the title of a Shakespeare play performed in theatres.

clue.text: Pessimist, one forecasting change of mood

parts.note: a prophet foretells the future

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters of mood are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gloomy forecaster predicting that people will shift in temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one forecasting' looks like part of the definition of a pessimist, but it is the prophet; 'change' alone is the anagram signal, and 'of' goes straight into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A doom-monger who constantly predicts disaster is a gloomy person who expects the worst.

clue.text: He deserts the poor upstanding soldiers

indicators.note: to desert is to leave, so those letters leave the word that follows
in a down clue standing up means reading from the bottom, backwards

explanation.surface: A man abandons the needy, who stand proudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He deserts the' leaves T; 'upstanding' turns POOR into ROOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of cavalry or a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Cockney conceals date mid-month

indicators.note: a Cockney, an East London speaker, is said to drop the H at the start of words

parts.note: to hide is to conceal

explanation.surface: A Londoner keeps a mid-month appointment secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney' drops the initial H from HIDES, as East Londoners are said to.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the fifteenth or thirteenth day of a month, made famous by Caesar's murder.

clue.text: Keep one first, one with gold, one with greater reason

indicators.note: this piece is placed before the word for keep

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, means one
a keep is a castle's stronghold, a fort
I is the Roman numeral for one
OR is the heraldic word for gold
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A castle comes first, then gold, for a stronger reason.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORTIORI is a Latin logic term for an argument that follows even more strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin logical phrase used when one claim follows even more strongly than another already accepted.

clue.text: Be reluctant with pop round about

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, dad
re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Hesitating with your father nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' is father here, not a drink or a bang; 'round' signals that word enclosing the short word for about.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear doing something makes one unwilling to face it.

clue.text: Not a new alliance

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: the two words as written are the letters to rearrange; that they also run backwards inside 'Not a new' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: This isn't a new coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is a military alliance of Western nations.

clue.text: I get pistol out in a flap!

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone gets a gun out while panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I GET PISTOL. 'in a flap' looks like panic, but the flap is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the cartilage lid at the back of the throat that closes over the windpipe during swallowing.
